claims.claim: Severian of Gabala was Bishop of Gabala in Syria.
Severian of Gabala flourished from around 400 until 404 as a popular preacher in Constantinople.
Severian of Gabala was born in Syria and spoke Greek with a Syriac accent.
Severian of Gabala became the enemy of John Chrysostom and helped condemn him at the Synod of the Oak.
Severian of Gabala composed a large number of commentaries on Holy Scripture, the whole being lost except for fragments in the Catenae.
The Fragmenta in epistulam ad Ephesios survives in catena tradition.
Severian's works can be found in the Clavis Patrum Graecorum nos. 4185-4295.
One of Severian's works was printed by Migne in the Patrologia Graeca 65.
Severian's homilies survive in Greek almost exclusively among the works of his enemy Chrysostom.
Severian was regarded by his contemporaries as a good preacher and was known as the author of Biblical commentaries and sermons.
Severian came to Constantinople about 400 provided with a series of Greek sermons.
